chunks: 1308 - What Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who shortens his prayers at his property, so he said: “There is no harm, so long as he has not intended a stay of ten days, unless he has there a house which he takes as a residence.”

He said: I said to him, “What is meant by residence?” He said: “That he has there a house in which he stays for six months. When it is like that, he completes his prayers there whenever he enters it.”

key_terms.الِاسْتِيطَانُ: residence or establishing oneself in a place
key_terms.ضَيْعَتِهِ: his property, estate, or rural holding
key_terms.مُقَامَ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: an intended stay of ten days
key_terms.يَسْتَوْطِنُهُ: he takes it as a place of residence
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he completes the prayer in full

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler complete prayer instead of shortening it at his property or residence?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on prayer during travel in relation to one’s property or dwelling. It explains that a person may shorten the prayer there unless he intends to stay ten days, but if he has an established residence there in the sense described by the Imam عليه السلام, then he performs the prayer in full whenever he enters it.
